column1: # The corpora, TAB-separated: name<TAB>path<TAB>reads<TAB>preset<TAB>purpose
# THE SEPARATOR IS A REAL TAB. Do not let an editor expand it.
# Both registered corpora are COMMITTED, which is the opposite of the isONclust
# and isONform registries, where the real data lived outside the repository.
# Two reasons it is the right call here and not there:
#   1. They are small. 390 KB and 5.2 MB against isONclust's multi-gigabyte
#      corpora. The repository has 520 MB of dead test data to strip (see
#      tools/repo-slim/); these two are not the problem.
#   2. They are already in HEAD and the README links both. Removing them would
#      break documentation for the sake of a registry convention.
# Path resolution: a path starting with `test/` is repo-relative; anything else
# is relative to $NGSPECIESID_DATA (default ~/data/amplicon); an absolute path
# is used as-is.
# WHICH ONE TO DEVELOP AGAINST
# `sup`. Measured over the 24-case matrix, `smoke` produces 12 distinct results
# and `sup` produces 19, and `smoke`'s single largest collision group is ELEVEN
# cases -- including --symmetric_map_align_thresholds, which is the only piece
# of clustering logic this port has to write from scratch. On `smoke` that flag
# changes nothing; on `sup` it gives 85 clusters against the default's 49.
# See PORTING.md, Finding 19. A green run on `smoke` alone is not coverage.
# PRIVATE CORPORA ARE NOT REGISTERED HERE
# The port is additionally verified against four corpora supplied by
# collaborators. They are NOT ours to publish and nothing derived from them is
# in this repository: not the reads, not the goldens (whose sample/ directory
# holds verbatim read heads and full ONT accessions), not the file names, and
# not the paths they came from.
# Register them in `bench/corpora.local.tsv`, same five columns, which is
# gitignored and which resolve_corpus reads after this file. Their goldens go
# under `bench/golden/private/`, also gitignored. Nothing else changes: the
# harness treats a local corpus exactly like a registered one.
# What may be said about them publicly is only what is true of the PORT: it is
# byte-identical on six corpora rather than two, across four read-length
# regimes rather than two. See PORTING.md, *The corpora*.
# WHAT IS MISSING
#   * A PacBio corpus. --isoseq is a supported preset with no data behind it,
#     and every corpus available here -- public or private -- is ONT. This is
#     the biggest hole by some distance.
#   * A corpus with a quality spread. On smoke and sup, --q 0 gives byte-
#     identical output to the default --q 7, so the filter is only observable
#     from --q 8 up, where it is already discarding most of the data.
#   * Reads with primers at KNOWN positions, so trimming can be checked against
#     an answer rather than against the reference's own output.
# ONE MORE IS AVAILABLE FOR FREE: test/terncytb_200.fastq, 200 real ONT reads of
# a Cytb/16S amplicon (median length 428, against 632 and 816 here), was
# committed in a2128c8 and dropped in 11c516f. It is 214 KB and it is the only
# strippable blob in this history NOT already archived, so it has to be handled
# either way -- restoring it costs less than archiving it. It does not
# discriminate --symmetric_map_align_thresholds. See tools/repo-slim/README.md.
# name
smoke
column5: committed, 390 KB. The README install check and .travis.yml's fixture. One haddock amplicon, `h1` in every header. Median length 632, and one read of length 14 that exercises the 2*k filter. BLIND TO FIVE PARAMETERS -- see Finding 19

column1: sup
column5: committed, 5.2 MB. The paper's Supplementary Data 1: cod, haddock and whiting on a Flongle, tagged c1/h1/w1 in every header. DEVELOP AGAINST THIS. Median length 816. 19 distinct results of 24 cases; reaches the reverse-complement merge path (4 draft centers, one merged) and primer trimming with the committed IUPAC primer file
